document.title: Let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control: an SDK client, the Host Companion, plugin packages, and a boot-time LAN Listener with Shell linking.
document.why: Per [PR #144](source:s1), a Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it.

sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unauthorized peers before reading their bodies**

When a non-linked LAN peer sends a slow or concurrent request, `reply` waits for `readBody` to finish before checking `isAllowed`; `readBody` continues consuming the stream and buffers up to 64 KiB per request, so denied peers can tie up sockets and memory before receiving a 403. Check the peer before reading the body, or abort unauthorized requests immediately, so the allowlist also protects availability.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

sources.label: matemolnar8 on PR #144
sources.author: matemolnar8
sources.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Máté Molnár**

Fixed in 04760101. `reply` now runs `isAllowed` before `readBody`. A peer that is not linked gets the 403 straight away, and `request.resume()` discards its body without buffering it. The peer-check tests in `test/server.test.ts` still pass (24/24).

sources.label: fix(shell): an empty Shell focuses Host Control so Cross keeps listening

lookFor: [#111](source:s4) asks for a separate link listener on port 8798 that runs only while the Shell Host Control Screen is open, stops after a link, and leaves Runtime Upload untouched. At head `POST /link` is a route on the LAN Listener at 8787, which `main.c` starts at boot, and the harness asserts it keeps running after a link. [PR #144](source:s1) says the separate listener felt clunky after testing.

[#109](source:s2) specifies a flat command registry: `host.<name>()`, an internal `defineHostCommands`, and `HostCapabilities.commands` as a `string[]`. At head commands live in public `defineHostPlugin` plugins, each request carries a `plugin` field, and capabilities lists `plugins`. [PR #144](source:s1) lists the plugin model as a deviation.

[#109](source:s2) names the getter `nativeGetHostControlUrl(): string`, and [#111](source:s4) stores one link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` returns a JSON array of up to 4 links from `host-control-links.json`, keyed by a companion `id`. [PR #144](source:s1) lists several links as a deviation.

[#109](source:s2) puts the SDK tests in `src/host-control/*.test.ts`, run by a new `test:sdk` script in the `fast` tier. At head they are `js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.ts`, picked up by widening the existing `test:cli` glob; no `test:sdk` script exists, and no source gives a reason.

[#110](source:s3) targets Node 22+, runs the companion from source with tsx, and keeps `{ port, advertise, vita, enable }` in its config. At head the published bin is a rolldown bundle whose README asks for Node.js 24, and the config holds `id`, `name`, `port`, `advertise` and a `vitas` array with no `enable`. [PR #145](source:s5) explains the bundle; no source gives the Node 24 floor.
[PR #144](source:s1) says the first `start` needs the computer's firewall prompt accepted, since the Vita connects in to port 8797; the companion README gives the macOS, Windows and Linux steps.

groups.title: Wire contract and plugin registry
groups.summary: `protocol.ts` fixes the wire codes and request shapes, and `plugin.ts` defines plugins that Deck Apps import and the companion implements. The ten JSON fixtures pin the bytes that the SDK, companion and C harness all replay.

attention.note: `ImplementedHostPlugin` (a string `id` plus a `ReadonlyMap` of `isPayload`/`run`) and `HOST_PLUGIN_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 are what a `.vdplugin` built with one SDK promises a companion of another. Each package bundles its own copy of this module, so the companion matches that shape, and `HostCommandError` by `name`, not by class. Renaming the error class or changing `commands` from a `Map` breaks every package already built.

notes.body: Events default to an empty map, so `watchHostEvents` offers no names for event-less plugins.

groups.title: Deck App client and event watching
groups.summary: `client.ts` turns a plugin into typed methods that resolve to `HostResult` and never reject, reading the links from `nativeGetHostControlLinks` on every call. `watchHostEvents` keeps one `core.events` wait open, passing `next` back as `after`.

attention.note: The Vita `fetch` has no `AbortSignal`, so `send` races the request against a 5 s timer and never retries. After a `timeout` the native request keeps running up to curl's 30 s cap, and the command may still run on the computer. `watchHostEvents` therefore waits 30 s before retrying a timed-out wait, and gives each wait 29 s against the companion's 25 s hold.

notes.body: Only the runtime's `runtime-native.d.ts` declares this getter; Deck App globals do not.

groups.title: Companion server and events
groups.summary: `startHostCompanion` serves `POST /command`, checking route, method, content type, size, version, plugin, command and payload guard in order, and `events.ts` holds `core.events` waits until the plugin emits. As [chatgpt-codex-connector asked](source:s6), `reply` checks the peer before reading the body.

attention.note: `isAllowed` answers every peer while the config's `vitas` list is empty, so a companion that was started but never linked serves any LAN host. Once linked, it answers those Vita IPs, loopback and this computer's own addresses, all spoofable. The built-ins only read, so today the exposure is `echo`, `notify`, system stats, and any installed custom plugin.

notes.body: `ok` is spread last, so a result field named `ok` cannot fake success.
An `after` past the current `seq` comes from before a restart; watching starts from now.

groups.title: Companion linking and relink
groups.why: [PR #144](source:s1) wants a new computer IP or port to reach linked Vitas without running `link` again.
groups.summary: `linkVita` checks that `start` answers on loopback, picks the interface routed to the Vita, and posts the link; `relink` in `cli.ts` replays it for each saved Vita on every `start`. A Vita that answers `unknown_link` is removed from `vitas`.

attention.note: The config stores Vita IPs without ports, and `relink` calls `linkVita(vita, …)`, which defaults to port 8787. A Vita whose LAN Listener fell forward to 8788 refuses the connection, which `linkVita` marks `retry: true`, so the companion retries it every 30 s for as long as it runs. The companion README says such a Vita needs `link` again.

notes.body: Re-reads the config so a `link` from another process is not overwritten.
Every attempt, retries included, chains on one promise, so config writes never overlap.

groups.title: Companion plugin packages
groups.why: [PR #145](source:s5) says a globally installed companion could not load a plugin installed somewhere else.
groups.summary: `plugin.ts` loads a `.vdplugin` folder by its manifest and unpacks a `.vdplugin.zip` safely, and `cli.ts` installs, removes, watches and reloads packages, keeping the previous set when a load fails. `cli.ts` also holds the relink code from the linking group.

attention.note: Each reload imports the package entry under a new `?v=<sha256>` query, so a rebuild is not served from the module cache. Node never unloads ESM modules, so a long `pnpm host` session keeps every rebuilt copy, with anything it allocated at module load, in memory. Lifecycle `stop` functions end timers, but module-level state stays.

notes.body: `--plugin` packages load last, so they replace an installed plugin with the same id.

groups.title: Native link store and getter
groups.summary: `link.c` parses `POST /link` bodies and keeps up to 4 links in `host-control-links.json`, newest first, and `jslib/host_control.c` exposes them as `nativeGetHostControlLinks`. `bootstrap.c` loads the store at boot and fails startup if it cannot.

attention.note: `host_control_links_save` puts a new companion id first and drops the oldest past `VD_HOST_CONTROL_MAX_LINKS` (4) without telling anyone. Linking a fifth computer silently forgets the least recently linked one. That companion's next `start` relink then gets `unknown_link` and removes this Vita from its config.

groups.summary: The upload server becomes `lan_listener.c` with a `POST /link` route, its HTTP helpers move to `src/net/http.c`, and `main.c` starts it at boot. [PR #144](source:s1) says the Vita VPK builds, but nothing was tested on hardware.

groups.title: Cancel fetches when a Deck App stops
groups.why: [PR #144](source:s1) needs a held event wait not to stall a reload.
groups.summary: `fetch_shutdown` marks every pending request cancelled, and the new curl progress callback aborts it. `js_limits_harness` stops a Deck App whose fetch waits on a server that never answers.

attention.note: curl aborts a cancelled transfer only at its next progress callback, about once a second. Stopping a Deck App can still wait about a second for held event waits, instead of up to 30 s. The progress callback, with its mutex lock, now runs on every Deck App fetch.

focus.caption: Stop must finish within 3 s while the fetch hangs.

fileNotes.tests/js_limits_harness.c: A silent loopback server; stopping took 15 s before the fix.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.
